findings.title: ZachXBT discloses Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as alleged victim of $133M crypto theft
findings.summary_md: Onchain investigator ZachXBT first identified Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a cryptocurrency theft estimated at more than $133 million, naming the bank on November 3, 2026. He traced withdrawals from several centralized exchange accounts and published Ethereum addresses he attributes to the theft, with funds allegedly swapped into ether and Monero. CoinDesk reported ZachXBT first put losses above $106 million before adding another $27 million in exchange withdrawals. The disclosure predates the bank's public confirmation by roughly two days.

findings.title: Euronews publishes mainstream coverage of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa cyberattack
findings.summary_md: Euronews reported on November 4, 2026 that Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed a cyberattack enabling fraudulent transactions while insisting customers would suffer no financial loss. The bank said it temporarily suspended certain transactions to block further fraudulent movements. According to Le Télégramme, $133 million (€118 million) was reportedly stolen, though the bank told Le Parisien the amount was still being assessed and some funds were frozen. The fraud was first made public by ZachXBT, an independent cryptocurrency investigator.

findings.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa vendor advisory on service-provider cyberattack
findings.summary_md: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's advisory states attackers entered through a service provider's platform and used the bank's own account to send transactions to other banking actors, with funds potentially converted into cryptocurrency. The bank explicitly denied any entry via Fortuneo and said clients face no financial consequences, with some funds frozen and a portion blocked. A prior press release was distributed on November 4 at 13:00 local time. The bank is working with judicial and police authorities to determine the attack's origin.
